sn10.5:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
sn10.5:1.2: Now on that occasion a certain female lay follower had a son named Sānu who had been possessed by a yakkha.
sn10.5:1.3: Then that female lay follower, lamenting, on that occasion recited these verses:
sn10.5:2.2: And on the eighths of the fortnight,
sn10.5:3.2: With those who lead the holy life,
sn10.5:3.3: The yakkhas do not sport around
sn10.5:3.4: So I have heard from the arahants.
sn10.5:3.5: But now today I see for myself
sn10.5:4.2: And on the eighths of the fortnight,
sn10.5:5.2: With those who lead the holy life
sn10.5:5.3: The yakkhas do not sport around
sn10.5:5.4: “What you heard from the arahants is good.
sn10.5:6.1: When Sānu has awakened tell him
sn10.5:6.3: Do not do an evil deed
sn10.5:7.1: If you should do an evil deed,
sn10.5:7.2: Or if you are doing one now
sn10.5:7.3: You won’t be free from suffering
sn10.5:7.4: Though you fly up and flee
sn10.5:8.1: They weep, mother, for the dead
sn10.5:8.2: Or for one living who isn’t seen
sn10.5:8.3: When you see, mother, that I’m alive
sn10.5:8.4: Why, O mother, do you weep for me?
sn10.5:9.1: They weep, O son, for the dead
sn10.5:9.2: Or for one living who isn’t seen
sn10.5:9.4: But when one returns to the home life
sn10.5:9.5: They weep for this one too, my son
sn10.5:9.6: For though alive he’s really dead.
sn10.5:10.1: Drawn out, my dear, from hot embers
sn10.5:10.2: You wish to plunge into hot embers
sn10.5:10.3: Drawn out, my dear, from an inferno
sn10.5:10.4: You wish to plunge into an inferno
sn10.5:11.1: Run forward, good luck be with you!
sn10.5:11.2: To whom could we voice our grief?
sn10.5:11.3: Being an item rescued from the fire
sn10.5:11.4: You wish to be burnt again.
